Evelyn —

Thanks for the intro earlier. PrimeConnect is preparing to onboard Redwood as a connector for AcmeHealth. Legal has two immediate asks before we move the PoC to pilot: a) confirmation on a documented contingency routing policy if EU-hosted capacity is constrained, and b) an editable DPA with your proposed redlines (we have our standard revisions attached).

Specifically, they want to understand whether Redwood can:
- guarantee in-region processing for PHI-derived telemetry, or failover to a specific onshore provider,
- provide a list of subprocessors that will touch the tokens/embeddings layer, and
- confirm whether SCCs cover the planned flow (controller-processor) together with any UK IDTA implications.

Can you share a short playbook and the DPA draft? We are on a tight timeline — legal has a review window next week.

Attachments: primeconnect_dpa_redlines_v1.pdf (pdf)

Best,
Susan

Hi Susan —

Thanks — this is very actionable. High level answers up-front, then attachments and next steps below.

Short answers:
- Residency: Redwood supports three serving modes: Hosted (multi-tenant), Dedicated (isolated GPU pools), and Private (VPC/on-prem). For your PHI-derived telemetry we recommend Dedicated or Private to meet the residency and access-control expectations.
- Contingency/failover: We can implement a deterministic fallback routing policy: primary EU dedicated pool -> secondary EU dedicated pool -> US onshore Dedicated (explicitly invoked only during capacity/incident conditions). We document the trigger thresholds and automatic rollback.
- Subprocessors: see attached draft DPA (section 4.2) for the current subprocessor list and delegation model; we will provide a CSV export of processors for the final contract.
- SCCs/UK IDTA: SCCs apply for standard EU->US flows; if you require UK-specific provisions we can include the UK addendum (we have a template). For the telem/data classification you described, we'll propose SCCs + UK addendum and a Technology Implementation Addendum (TIA) that enumerates permitted cross-border paths.

Attachments: redwood-primeconnect-dpa-draft.docx (docx), routing-diagram.png (png)

Proposed next step: 30-min triage call Wednesday 08/19 with legal + infra to align on the failover thresholds and finalize the DPA redlines. Two proposed times: 09:30 or 14:00 PT. Which works?

—Evelyn Hart
Director, Partner Integrations
Redwood Inference

Evelyn / team —

Thanks for the clear draft. A few legal ops clarifications before I sign off to send back to PrimeConnect:

1) Role mapping: Confirm whether PrimeConnect will be a controller and Redwood a processor for the telemetry data. If PrimeConnect is acting as a controller of PHI-derived telemetry, SCCs are the right mechanism. If there's joint-controller activity we need to map responsibilities in an exhibit.

2) Subprocessor granularity: The DPA lists "inference infra providers" and "storage brokers" — please expand to explicit vendor names (or mark as "to be confirmed") and provide a one-line justification for each. Procurement will want vendor-level attestations for encryption and access controls.

3) Failover SLA: the routing diagram looks good, but we need a short clause capturing the activation conditions (CPU/GPU utilization thresholds, incident signal sources) and a maximum outbound residency exposure window (e.g., no more than 4 hours offshore without manual approval).

4) TIA scope: For the TIA, include a table with the permitted technical paths and the KV cache behavior (to prevent accidental token leaks across regions).

If infra can draft the minimal language for the SLA/activation conditions, I can fold into the DPA and return to PrimeConnect legal.

—Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Data Protection
Redwood Inference

Laura/Kim/Jonas/Susan —

Quick dispatch with decisions and actions from this thread and the triage call (notes below). Thank you all for the fast turnaround.

Decisions:
- Role mapping: PrimeConnect is controller; Redwood will act as processor for telemetry and embeddings. SCCs + UK addendum + TIA will be the chosen package.
- Subprocessors: We will provide a vendor CSV and a short attestation for each named vendor (encryption at rest, key custody, access control). Current critical subprocessors enumerated in the DPA are: ManagedGPU Ops (in-eu-dedicated), ObjectStoreCo (eu-storage), and MetricsBroker (telemetry pipelines).
- Failover SLA: infra confirmed an automatic fallback path with a maximum of 3 hours offshore exposure (we tightened from 4 hrs). Activation signals: sustained >85% dedicated pool utilization for 10 minutes OR explicit capacity incident flagged by SRE. Manual approval resets will be required for >3 hour offshore windows.

Actions:
- Laura: fold the SLA activation clause into section 5.3 of the DPA and re-export to Word track changes (due EOD 08/20).
- Kim: produce the subprocessor CSV and single-line attestations (due 08/20).
- Jonas/Infra: publish the routing playbook in the shared drive and add runbook IDs to the TIA (Jonas to post link).
- Evelyn: send updated DPA + diagram to PrimeConnect legal after Laura's redline incorporated.

Attachments included in this email: redwood-primeconnect-dpa-draft.docx (docx) — latest with infra notes, routing-diagram.png

Next touchpoints: Laura to upload redlined DPA by 08/20; we aim for signature window 08/24-08/26 (DocuSign link to follow).
